name: Pleated trousers

card.summary: Trousers with fabric folds below the waistband that add room through the hips and thighs, giving a fuller, more comfortable fit and a classic or retro silhouette.
card.note: Fit depends on cut; fashion cycles have moved pleats in and out of style.

quick.overview:
Pleated trousers have one or more folds of fabric sewn in just below the waistband at the front. The folds release when you sit or move, adding room across the hips and thighs, which is why they are associated with comfortable, roomy fits.

For looks, they change the silhouette of the lower half: a fuller leg that tapers toward the ankle suits people with larger thighs or glutes, and the style carries a classic tailored or vintage association. Fashion has cycled in and out of favour with them.
quick.how: Wearers pick between single, double or triple pleats and between forward pleats, which open toward the zipper, and reverse pleats, which open toward the pockets. They are typically paired with a tucked or half-tucked top, belt or suspenders, and tailored to the right rise and hem.
quick.risks: There are no health risks. The practical caveat is fit: a pleated style cut too full for the wearer can look bulky, and the look is seen differently by different style communities.

lead: Pleated trousers are trousers whose front has one, two or three folds of fabric just under the waistband; the pleat can open toward the pockets (reverse pleat) or toward the crotch (forward pleat) [1]. Flat-front styles such as jeans and cargo pants contrast with them [1].

Their appeal for appearance is the shape they give. Pleats serve both practical and stylistic purposes, including freedom of movement [1], and tailors use them to add volume at the hips and thighs while the leg tapers below. People with muscular legs or a larger lower body sometimes use pleated cuts for fit and comfort.

Pleated trousers were popular before World War II, common in the 1980s and 1990s as double reverse pleats, fell out of favour by the late 2000s, and were the subject of a 2018 article anticipating a return [1]. A T Nation forum exchange shows how gym culture treated them as office wear rather than gym wear [2].

chain: Pleats add fabric at the front of the hips and thighs
More room and a fuller line through the upper leg
Comfortable fit and a classic or vintage silhouette
angle.text: The folds provide extra room over the thighs and hips so the trouser drapes rather than clings. Wearers use them for comfort and for a relaxed, tailored look.

paras: Pleats are sewn folds that sit under the front waistband; trousers can have none, one, two or three [1]. Reverse pleats open toward the pockets and are typical on khakis and corduroy trousers, whereas forward pleats open toward the crotch [1].

Pleats were widespread before World War II. In the 1980s and 1990s double reverse pleats were common, and by the late 2000s they had declined in popularity [1]. A 2018 Bloomberg article, cited on Wikipedia, discussed a possible return [1].

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and gym culture
paras: In a 2008 T Nation thread about gym clothing, one poster remarked that pleats do not fit in at the gym, reflecting their association with office and casual dress [2]. A separate T Nation thread on casual clothes for work gives menswear advice from a custom-clothing business owner [3].

timeline.event: Pleated trousers are widely worn before World War II [1].
A Bloomberg article discusses the return of pleated pants [1].
